sources.title: Introducing Grok 4.7
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. September 21 release announcement explicitly identifies a new, larger base than Grok 4.6, followed by longer reinforcement learning. No numerical parameter count or dense/MoE classification is supplied; it does not contradict the founder-announced 2.1T nominal size.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 model specification
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact grok-4.7 model page retains text/image input, text output, 500000 context and four reasoning efforts. It provides no numerical parameter count or network topology.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 Model Card, revision 2026-09-21
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The 30-page September 21 card describes pretraining, supplemental training, SFT and RL; Grok 4.6 generated SFT trajectories, which is not same-base lineage. Full-text parameter search finds no count. Pages 3-4 disclose neither active parameters nor dense/MoE routing. No pruning, expert expansion or change contradicting the announced nominal size is described.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 Model Card, earlier public file
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The earlier 30-page September 21 card has the same substantive training description and no parameter-count disclosure. It provides no alternative nominal size, active count or dense/MoE classification.

sources.title: Elon Musk original Grok 4.6 / Grok 4.7 scale post, July 28, 2026
sources.evidence: Re-fetched original X syndication JSON October 27, 2026. Author elonmusk (user 44196397), post 2082123925283041545, timestamp 2026-07-28T15:20:02Z. The founder explicitly names Grok 4.7 as a 2.1T model, a primary nominal model-size disclosure. It does not provide a separate active count, counting convention or exact deployed tensor count. The post is truncated after later capability claims, but the numerical disclosure is intact. Canonical post: https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2082123925283041545.

sources.title: API release notes: September 21, 2026
sources.evidence: Exact September 21 entry announces grok-4.7 availability on the xAI API with 500k context, text/image input, text output, and four reasoning efforts. Fast is expressly the same model on faster serving infrastructure, rather than another checkpoint.

sources.title: Grok 4.7 developer guide
sources.evidence: Rechecked October 27, 2026. Exact developer guide lists grok-4.7, 500000-token context, text/image input, text output and function calling. Fast is the same model on faster infrastructure. No total/active parameter count or network architecture is disclosed.

sources.title: Reasoning: Grok 4.7 controls
sources.evidence: Names grok-4.7 specifically, lists effort controls, states that reasoning cannot be disabled, and describes encrypted reasoning returned by its Responses API.

sources.title: Files Overview
sources.evidence: Attaching a file activates attachment_search and creates an agentic document-search workflow. PDF handling through this interface is not evidence for native PDF input to the underlying model.

sources.title: Enterprise Terms of Service, updated August 14, 2026
sources.evidence: Sections 1.1 and 4.1 grant limited hosted-service/API access and retain ownership of underlying models and technology. Supports descriptive proprietary classification for the hosted model; no model-weight license is granted.

sources.title: Official xai-org public model inventory
sources.evidence: Accessed inventory contains xai-org/grok-1 and xai-org/grok-2, not Grok 4.7. Used with its documented hosted distribution and proprietary terms, not as standalone proof from search absence.

sources.title: Cursor Grok 4.7 model and training overview
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Cursor says it jointly trained Grok 4.7 with SpaceXAI on a new, larger base than Grok 4.6, followed by longer reinforcement learning. No numerical size or dense/MoE structure is supplied; no same-base inheritance from Grok 4.6 is justified.

sources.title: Grok 4.7: Cursor model help
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact-model help identifies a jointly built first-party model with a larger base and longer training. It does not identify a numerically specified base checkpoint or disclose parameter counts or routing.

sources.title: Introducing Grok 4.7: Cursor release post
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026. September 21 developer post links to the xAI announcement as the full release description. It adds no parameter count, active count or named-base lineage. Searches for exact-model size, 2.1T, active parameters and architecture across xAI, Cursor and original founder posts found no newer first-party numerical disclosure.

name.note: Exact public product name and API identifier.

developer.note: The card expressly allows xAI and SpaceXAI interchangeably and identifies the developer; retain the established xAI catalog identity despite current SpaceXSI branding. Cursor separately confirms joint development; record this collaboration without changing the catalog developer key.

family.note: Named Grok release and successor to Grok 4.6.

release_date.note: Same-day primary API/product release announcement. Earlier founder roadmap dates were forecasts, not public availability; later provider listings do not replace this date.

open_weights.note: Documented hosted model, with proprietary service terms and no public Grok 4.7 checkpoint in the official weight inventory.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the closed hosted model under developer service terms, rather than an open-weight license identifier.

parameters_b.note: Accept 2100B as the founder-published nominal model size for the exact Grok 4.7 name, preserving the 2.1T precision of the July 28 primary disclosure. The source predates release; the public note preserves that limitation. A nominal specification does not require an exact deployed tensor count or repetition in the launch card. Fresh October 27 review found no superseding numerical size or contradictory structural change in the launch, both cards, training update or current developer references. The statement does not specify component accounting or active parameters; do not present 2100B as an exact tensor census. The new larger base and Grok 4.6-generated SFT data do not support inheriting sibling sizes.

active_parameters_b.note: Re-audited October 27, 2026. The founder nominal-size post, later training update, both model cards, launch materials and current xAI/Cursor references provide no separate active-per-token count or routing specification. Exact-model searches found no newer first-party active-count disclosure. The 2.1T overall nominal size, new larger-base description, SFT teacher and faster serving do not establish active parameters; retain null rather than equating active with nominal size.

architecture.note: The launch establishes a different, larger base than Grok 4.6; training descriptions do not establish dense/MoE routing, Transformer layout, layers, attention or experts. Targeted searches for exact-model developer training/interpretability research and original researcher posts found no further structural disclosure. Do not inherit Grok 4.5/4.6 topology. Cursor confirms a new larger base; its MoE kernel paper describes Composer, and its September 23 research concerns the harness rather than this model network.

context_window.note: Native xAI context limit, independently confirmed in the exact model payload. Cursor exposes a 256k standard product tier and 500k long context, consistent with retaining the native maximum.

modalities.note: Remove PDF from direct inputs: uploaded documents invoke attachment_search. Producing documents, images or code-executed artifacts through tools does not add native output modalities.

reasoning.note: Exact model supports low, medium, high and xhigh effort, defaults to high, and cannot disable reasoning.

tool_call.note: Exact model feature flag and developer guide establish function calling; server tools include web search, X search and code execution.

description.value: Grok reasoning model for coding, agentic tasks and knowledge work, with text and image input, text output and configurable reasoning effort.
description.note: Replace frontier-ranking language with documented purpose, modalities and configurable reasoning.

patch.notes: Released on the xAI API September 21, 2026. Text and image inputs are native; PDF attachments use search. The nominal 2.1T size comes from Elon Musk's July 28 pre-release announcement for Grok 4.7. Released model cards do not independently confirm the final count, and no superseding figure was found. Active parameters and network architecture remain undisclosed. The new base and Grok 4.6-generated training data do not establish shared model size. Reasoning cannot be disabled and supports low, medium, high and xhigh. Grok 4.7 Fast serves the same model faster. Cursor's standard 256k product tier does not replace the native 500k context maximum.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit accepts the directly re-accessed founder 2.1T disclosure as 2100B nominal size, with explicit founder-announced scope and primary_source provenance. Fresh review of both model cards, the launch, original training/launch posts and current xAI/Cursor references found no superseding numerical specification. Active parameters and architecture remain undisclosed; no sibling size or topology is inherited. Earlier non-parameter corrections are preserved.
